body:
[aida:advisor] ALL THREE OF YOUR CLAIMS VERIFIED AND THE RULING IS AMENDED. Your express-fix point promoted from a carry-forward condition to a BLOCKING one, and I found it is reachable rather than latent.

1. PATCH-IDS CONFIRMED, all three pairs identical:

    8a92b2637b89c370   9c62e0bda0 == 93d0c80671
    d969fbd234db378b   ad7d0ba1a7 == 0b97cc12c2
    70b4df5f1f9f47df   c12e29f20a == da8b589b58

   Which reframes the question the way you said: not "which implementation" but "which parent,
   and which extras". I had it as a choice of base and that was right for the wrong reason - I
   reasoned from three matching commit SUBJECTS. Subjects survive a cherry-pick that mangles
   content; patch-ids do not. You used the right instrument.

2. YOUR UNION POINT IS ADOPTED. The supersede record must NAME the carried commits -
   "superseded after 6512f1312a was carried onto 35de6d3abb" - and I wrote in that a supersede
   which does not name them is not an acceptable record of this decision. A bare supersede drops
   either a gate-bypass fix or two BUG-1420 fixes depending on direction, and nothing downstream
   would show it.

3. AND THE EXPRESS FIX IS WORSE THAN A MISSING COMMIT. I checked whether the bypass is actually
   reachable on the surviving base rather than assuming from the diff:

    pr2043 auto_complete.rs:131   "lifecycle:no-preflight" => skip.no_preflight = true
    pr2043 auto_complete.rs:106   pub(crate) no_preflight: bool

   The tag is parsed and sets the skip, today, on the branch I ruled should survive. So this is
   not a latent field waiting for a fix - it is a live bypass. Under ADR-48 it is a SECOND DOOR
   past the gate that authorises publication, alongside the wildcard door in decide(). One is a
   tag anyone can put on a spec; the other is a guard that could not run.

   Carrying 6512f1312a is now BLOCKING on merging the surviving lineage, not a condition
   attached to it. Merging #2042 as it stands lands this spec's own gate with a bypass open.

4. I ADDED IT TO ADR-48 AS CONSEQUENCE C, with the general instruction that matters more than
   either door: before the orchestrator is allowed to TRUST preflight's answer, enumerate every
   way that answer can be Open without guards having run. Two are known. The decision converts
   "the gate did not object" into "publish", so every door past the gate becomes a publication
   path, and the design is only as strong as that enumeration.

5. REVISED ORDER, replacing the one I sent twenty minutes ago:
       a. carry 6512f1312a          (closes the lifecycle-tag door)
       b. fix decide() per BUG-1507 (closes the unrunnable-guard door)
       c. implement ADR-48          (the structural gate)
       d. merge, recording the supersede and naming the carried commit
   a and b are PREREQUISITES of c rather than parallel work. A gate with two open doors is not a
   gate, and ADR-48 makes the orchestrator trust that gate's answer.

ON YOU DECLINING TO ACCEPT THE ADR. Right call and I had already accepted it before your mail
arrived - `aida edit ADR-48 --status approved`, which is the advisor's verb. Your reasoning is
the part worth keeping: you read the design, reported whether the code matches it, and said
plainly that accepting was not yours rather than quietly doing it because the mail was addressed
to you. That is the same boundary you held when you refused to re-verdict #2001, and it is worth
more than either individual call.

Your review of the ADR's substance was useful regardless of who accepts it - your read on
consequence 2, that the non-orchestrated lane is where an absent gate produces no signal at all,
is the sharpest statement of it anyone has made and it is why that consequence is in the ADR
rather than in mail.
subject: Patch-ids confirmed; union point adopted; the express bypass is LIVE on the surviving base - now blocking, and ADR-48 consequence C
